extraction.name: FOMO60K
extraction.description: A large-scale, heterogeneous dataset of 60,529 brain Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI) scans from 13,900 sessions and 11,187 subjects, aggregated from 16 publicly available sources. The dataset includes both clinical- and research-grade images, multiple MRI sequences, and a wide range of anatomical and pathological variability, including scans with large brain anomalies.
extraction.creator: Asbjørn Munk, Stefano Cerri, Jakob Ambsdorf, Julia Machnio, Sebastian Nørgaard Llambias, Vardan Nersesjan, Christian Hedeager Krag, Peirong Liu, Pablo Rocamora García, Mostafa Mehdipour Ghazi, Mikael Boesen, Michael Eriksen Benros, Juan Eugenio Iglesias, and Mads Nielsen
extraction.citeAs: Munk, A., Cerri, S., Ambsdorf, J., et al. (2025). A large-scale heterogeneous 3D magnetic resonance brain imaging dataset for self-supervised learning. arXiv:2506.14432.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The dataset was aggregated from 16 publicly available sources. Minimal preprocessing was applied to preserve the original image characteristics while reducing barriers to entry for new users.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: 16 publicly available datasets including MGH Wild, SOOP, BraTS-GEN, OASIS1, OASIS2, MSD Braintumor, IXI, NIMH, DLBS, IDEAS, ARC, MBSR, UCLA, QTAB, NKI, and AOMIC ID1000.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: MRI preprocessing comprised three main steps: reorienting images to RAS (Right–Anterior–Superior) orientation, affine co-registration, and skull-stripping. All scans were first reoriented to RAS and affinely co-registered using the mri_coreg command from FreeSurfer 7.4.130. Within each MRI session, scans were aligned to the image with the highest spatial resolution. For diffusion-weighted imaging (DWI) scans stored in 4D format, if a b=0 volume was available, it was extracted and saved separately. For the b=1000 shell, three diffusion-weighted volumes were selected based on their gradient directions being most closely aligned with the canonical x, y, and z axes, and averaged to produce a single representative 3D image. Skull-stripping was performed using SynthSeg. Skull-stripping was only applied when the images were not already defaced or skull-stripped by the dataset provider, or when visual inspection identified residual cranial features. Subjects have been shuffled to protect privacy.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Minimal preprocessing was applied to retain the raw characteristics of the original images while improving usability. Steps included reorienting to RAS, affine co-registration, and skull-stripping/defacing where necessary. MRI scans are stored in NIfTI-compressed format and organized using a standardized directory structure.
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The dataset will continue to grow in future releases as additional cohorts and modalities become available.
extraction.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: None explicitly stated, though subjects have been shuffled to protect privacy and prevent easy identification of dataset sources.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: FOMO60K is intended to support the development and benchmarking of self-supervised learning methods in medical imaging at scale, addressing the lack of large and diverse public datasets in neuroimaging which has slowed the adoption of SSL approaches.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The dataset aggregates data from 16 sources with varying protocols. Some sequence metadata was unknown or could not be reliably identified. Access to original sources may have been restricted by formal applications, data use agreements, and institutional approvals, although FOMO60K itself is publicly available.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Training, Testing, Validation, Fine Tuning. The dataset can be used with no further pre-processing for pre-training. It is intended to support the development and benchmarking of self-supervised learning methods in medical imaging at scale.
